publications.title: An Enterprise AI Assurance Framework for Biomedical Diagnostics: Integrating a Human Validation Boundary and a Multidimensional Assurance Score into a Lifecycle Governance Model.
publications.abstract: This paper presents the Enterprise AI Assurance Framework for Biomedical Diagnostics (EAIA-BD), a design-science framework combining a five-layer architecture, a Human Validation Boundary that specifies when and by whom AI outputs must be reviewed, the Biomedical AI Assurance Score (BAAS) with a safety-critical gate, and a seven-stage assurance lifecycle with a maturity model. The paper reports an analytical comparison with healthcare-AI frameworks and standards, standards mapping, a worked example, and score sensitivity analysis. These analyses do not constitute independent or empirical clinical validation: the framework has not been empirically validated, and no improvement in clinical safety, decision-making, diagnostic performance, or regulatory readiness is claimed.

An Enterprise AI Assurance Framework for Biomedical Diagnostics: Integrating a Human Validation Boundary and a Multidimensional Assurance Score into a Lifecycle Governance Model. publications.title: BQEB: A Reproducibility-First Architecture for Modular Energy AI Benchmarking
publications.abstract: The paper presents the BQEB Reproducibility Architecture, a four-layer framework for organizing energy-AI research artifacts, deterministic execution, checksummed evidence, benchmark evolution, version management, and scientific lineage. Within-environment deterministic execution was verified through 15 real executions, and checksum-based tamper detection was confirmed. Cross-environment reproducibility, statistical significance of model comparisons, and broader extensibility remain pending or future work; the paper also documents an unresolved numerical discrepancy between two published versions of a benchmark result as a governance case.

publications.title: Dynamic Constitutional Control of Agentic Enterprise Digital Twins via Meta-Governor Agents
publications.abstract: This paper proposes a Dynamic Constitutional Control framework for Agentic Enterprise Digital Twins, using Meta-Governor Agents to continuously supervise, constrain, and adapt autonomy policies. It translates enterprise governance principles into machine-enforceable control rules for escalation thresholds, action boundaries, rollback, and human approval checkpoints. The published evaluation reports experimental benchmarking on a synthetic enterprise governance dataset; it does not establish real-world enterprise deployment.

publications.title: AI-Driven Cloud Computing: Predictive vs. Conventional Resource Management
publications.abstract: Cloud Computing allows one to scale resources up or down on demand, yet the practice-oriented resource management methods currently used are not always capable of responding promptly to the changing needs. The emerging concept of Artificial Intelligence (AI) may offer a solution due to its unique ability to predict future demands. The present paper explores the concept of using AI in Cloud Computing and how it can address the current issues related to resource management, workload, and response time, scalability, security, and cost. A conceptual framework was created and evaluated within the experiment to identify whether an AI-based approach could be better than the status quo. A comparison was made between the traditional threshold-based provisioning and a newly designed predictive model through a simulated workload. On average, the experimental results showed a 32% decrease in response time, an increase in utilization from 64% to 81%, a reduction in scaling reaction delay by over 56%, and a reduction in operational cost by approximately 17%. Altogether, the experiment proved that predictive AI-based resource management can offer significant advantages over conventional methods in Cloud Computing, although there are factors that need to be considered for practical applications.

publications.title: TAEIR: Trust-Aware Edge Intelligence for Proactive ICU Risk Management
publications.abstract: Intensive-care monitoring remains dominated by single-parameter threshold alarms, of which the large majority are non-actionable and which contribute to alarm fatigue and delayed response. Machine-learning early-warning systems trained on retrospective ICU databases have demonstrated strong discrimination for sepsis and circulatory failure, yet independent evaluations of widely deployed proprietary models show that discrimination in one cohort does not translate into calibrated, trustworthy alerts in another. Building on the authors' earlier IoT/Edge-AI Smart ICU Monitoring System, this paper proposes TAEIR (Trust-Aware Edge Intelligence for ICU Risk), a nine-layer framework addressing predictive uncertainty, calibration, explanation, drift, and the governance mechanisms clinicians need in order to trust an alert. This is a framework, methodology, and benchmark-design paper reporting no experimental results, hardware measurements, or clinical outcomes.

publications.title: Trustworthy AI-Driven Hospital Digital Twin Framework for Resource Allocation and Patient Flow Optimization
publications.abstract: Hospitals worldwide face increasing operational complexity due to emergency department congestion, fluctuating patient demand, limited resources, and the need for real-time decision support. This paper proposes a Trustworthy AI-Driven Hospital Digital Twin Framework for intelligent resource allocation and patient flow optimization, integrating artificial intelligence forecasting, optimization algorithms, reinforcement learning, digital twin simulation, and AI assurance mechanisms into a unified operational intelligence architecture. The framework consists of five major layers: Hospital Data Integration, AI Prediction, Hospital Digital Twin, Decision Intelligence, and AI Assurance, establishing a research framework for trustworthy AI-enabled hospital operations.
